Specialisation:
Ophthalmology, cataract, corneal disease

Description:
Professor Uri Elbaz is a leading specialist in ophthalmology, with a focus on corneal disease and cataract. He heads the clinic for disorders of the anterior segment of the eye and cataract at the Schneider hospital, and runs private ophthalmology clinics in Tel Aviv.

Professional experience:

  • Head of private ophthalmology clinics in Tel Aviv
  • Head of the clinic for disorders of the anterior segment of the eye and cataract in children at the Schneider hospital
  • Leading physician of the ophthalmology department at the Beilinson medical centre
  • Specialisation in disorders of the anterior segment of the eye in children and in paediatric eye surgery, Toronto, Canada
  • Specialisation in corneal disease and cataract, Toronto, Canada
  • Specialisation in ophthalmology at the Assaf Harofeh hospital
  • Professor in the department of ophthalmology, Tel Aviv University
  • Engaged in research in ophthalmology

Education:

  • Graduate of the faculty of medicine, Tel Aviv University

Membership:

  • Israel Medical Association
  • Israel Ophthalmological Society
  • Israel Society for Vision and Eye Research
  • American Society of Cataract and Refractive Surgery
  • American Academy of Ophthalmology

Languages:

  • Hebrew
  • English

Areas of diagnosis and treatment:

  • Diseases of the cornea
  • Corneal insufficiency
  • Scarring after infection
  • Keratoconus
  • Transplantation of an artificial cornea
  • Cataract removal
  • Laser cataract surgery
  • Freedom from glasses
  • Laser refractive surgery
  • Paediatric ophthalmology
  • Congenital conditions and states following injury
  • Removal of dermoids in children
  • Disorders of the anterior segment of the eye in children
  • Corneal transplantation
  • Cross-linking
  • Pterygium removal

Ophthalmologist, paediatrician, surgeon

Main areas of specialisation

  • Treatment of squint in children and adults by conservative and surgical methods
  • Treatment of blocked tear ducts
  • Treatment of retinal detachment
  • Treatment of cataract and glaucoma in children
  • Surgery for uveitis

Summary

Professor Yair Morad is a physician of the highest category, an excellent ophthalmologist and head of a paediatric ophthalmology department. In more than 30 years of practice Professor Morad has published more than 45 research papers on various aspects of paediatric ophthalmology. His expert opinion and his approach to treatment are valued both in Israel and beyond.

Education

  • Faculty of medicine, Technion, with distinction
  • Military service as head of the medical service at the Ministry of Defence
  • Fellowship at the Schneider children's clinic
  • Specialisation at the children's hospital in Toronto, Canada

Languages

  • Hebrew
  • English

Membership of international associations

  • Israel Ophthalmological Society
  • Israel Society of Paediatric Ophthalmology
  • American Association for Pediatric Ophthalmology and Strabismus

Oncologist, dermatologist, dermato-oncologist

Main areas of specialisation:

Professor Jacob Schachter is a leading dermatologist and dermato-oncologist in Israel with many years of experience, recognised as one of the world's best specialists in the diagnosis and treatment of skin cancer.

  • Skin conditions
  • Research and treatment of melanoma
  • Treatment of skin cancer
  • Squamous cell carcinoma of the skin
  • Basal cell carcinoma
  • Ocular melanoma

Summary:

Professor Jacob Schachter is a leading dermatologist and dermato-oncologist in Israel with almost 40 years of experience. He specialises in the diagnosis and treatment of skin cancer, and of melanoma in particular. An innovator, he founded and heads the Ella Centre, which specialises in developing innovative treatments for melanoma and skin cancer.

Professor Schachter sees patients from around the world every day and achieves strong results with the treatment he prescribes. In his work he uses advanced methods of clinical oncology and radiation therapy, and actively develops and tests new approaches to treating melanoma. He has almost entirely stopped using chemotherapy and has considerably reduced the use of radiation therapy thanks to innovative targeted drugs.

Professor Schachter is also actively engaged in research in dermato-oncology. Under his direction an international research group was set up to conduct early clinical trials in melanoma. Among the group's developments is the newest TIL therapy, considered one of the most promising available today.

Education and clinical experience:

  • Faculty of medicine: Tel Aviv University, Israel
  • Faculty of medicine: Hebrew University of Jerusalem, Israel
  • Fellowship in oncology and radiation therapy: Rabin Medical Centre, Petah Tikva, Israel
  • Specialisation in dermato-oncology and radiotherapy: Beilinson Medical Centre, Petah Tikva, Israel

Academic and research work:

Professor Schachter is the author of more than 200 research papers on the treatment of benign and malignant skin growths. He teaches in the department of oncology in the faculty of medicine at Tel Aviv University. He holds many prestigious awards and grants for his achievements in cancer research and for developing innovative treatments for melanoma.

Membership of international associations:

  • Israel Society of Clinical Oncology and Radiation Therapy (ISCORT)
  • Israel melanoma association
  • European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer (EORTC)
  • International research group for early clinical trials in melanoma

Languages:

  • Hebrew
  • English

Professor Jacob Schachter is included among the best doctors in Israel and continues to contribute actively to medical science and practice.

Gynaecologist
Experience: 35 years

Specialisation:

Professor Yuval Yaron is one of Israel's leading obstetricians and gynaecologists. He currently combines heading the prenatal diagnosis department of the Ichilov-Sourasky medical complex with clinical work at the Assuta clinic. Besides obstetrics and gynaecology, Professor Yaron specialises in in vitro fertilisation and the prenatal diagnosis of genetic disorders.

  • IVF
  • Ovarian cyst
  • Infertility
  • Cervical dysplasia

Education and clinical experience:

  • 2018: Head of the prenatal diagnosis department, Ichilov (Sourasky) clinic
  • 2014: Senior physician, department of gynaecology and obstetrics, Ichilov (Sourasky) clinic
  • 2009: Physician, IVF department, Wayne State clinic in Detroit (USA)
  • 2008: Physician, medical genetics department, Ichilov (Sourasky) clinic
  • 2003: Physician, IVF department, HaKirya medical centre (Tel Aviv)
  • 2000: Head of obstetric ultrasound, Sheba medical centre (Israel)
  • 1997: Physician, gynaecology department, HaKirya medical centre (Tel Aviv)
  • 1995: Fellowship in medical genetics at Wayne State University, Michigan, USA
  • 1993: Physician, gynaecology department, Assaf Harofeh medical centre (Israel)
  • 1992: Fellowship in the IVF department of the Serlin maternity hospital, HaKirya, Tel Aviv
  • 1988: Sackler Faculty of Medicine, Tel Aviv University

Academic and research work:

After completing his studies in the faculty of medicine at Tel Aviv University, Yuval Yaron was sent to specialise in gynaecology at the large HaKirya maternity hospital in Tel Aviv. At the start of his career Dr Yaron worked as a physician in the gynaecology departments of two medical centres, Assaf Harofeh and HaKirya. He then headed the ultrasound unit of the department of gynaecology and obstetrics at the Sheba Tel HaShomer medical centre.

Yuval Yaron took his specialisation in medical genetics at the Wayne State University medical centre (Detroit, USA) and stayed on to work as a physician in the IVF department.

On returning to Israel, Dr Yaron began teaching at Tel Aviv University, where he subsequently became a professor in the department of obstetrics and gynaecology. Yuval Yaron combines teaching with research and continues to work with the Wayne State medical centre, where he was a member of a research group on prenatal genetics.

Yuval Yaron's research is published in many respected international professional journals. His work on the clinical presentation of Rett syndrome in men with MECP2 mutations, and on preimplantation genetic diagnosis in Canavan disease, has attracted particular interest.

Membership of medical associations:

  • Israel Fertility Association
  • Israel Association of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists
  • American Society of Human Genetics
  • Israel Society of Medical Genetics, which he chaired for a time

Urologist, venereologist, specialist in sexual medicine

Main areas of specialisation:

  • Urology
  • Andrology
  • Sexual medicine
  • Conditions of the urinary and reproductive organs
  • Diseases of the prostate (prostatitis, benign prostatic hyperplasia and others)
  • Treatment of erectile dysfunction
  • Reconstructive surgery of the male reproductive organs
  • Transurethral resection of the prostate
  • Diagnosis and treatment of cancer of the adrenal glands, kidneys, ureter, bladder and prostate

Summary:

Professor Yuza Chen is one of Israel's leading specialists in urology, andrology and sexual medicine, and a recognised expert in the treatment of sexual dysfunction and various sexual disorders. He is director of the sexual dysfunction clinic and a leading urologist at Assuta, Israel's largest clinic. He also holds the post of vice-president of the Israeli society of sexual medicine. Professor Chen has more than 40 years of experience.

Over his long clinical practice, Professor Yuza Chen has helped thousands of patients from around the world with conditions of the reproductive and urinary systems. He successfully treats cancers of the kidneys, adrenal glands, ureter, bladder and prostate. He helps not only men with erectile dysfunction but also women with various sexual disorders.

Professor Chen is a specialist of the highest class in reconstructive surgery, making active use of the most modern methods in oncological and reconstructive urological surgery.

Besides his daily clinical work, Professor Yuza Chen is actively engaged in research. He takes part in studies and development work on the newest treatments for urological conditions. The professor has extensive experience of working with leading medical centres in the United States, Israel, England, Austria, Singapore and Germany.

Professor Chen is also an excellent teacher at Tel Aviv University and presents research papers at various international professional congresses and forums. His opinion is valued highly by colleagues in the field. He is the author of two books and numerous papers on various problems in urology.

He has repeatedly received prestigious prizes and awards for his outstanding contribution to uro-oncology worldwide and to the treatment of erectile dysfunction.

Education:

  • Faculty of medicine, Nalchik university, Russia
  • Residency in surgery at the First Medical Institute in St Petersburg, Russia
  • Fellowship at the Ichilov medical centre, Tel Aviv, Israel
  • Fellowships at major medical centres in England, Austria, Singapore, Germany and the United States

Languages:

  • Hebrew
  • English
  • Russian

Membership of international associations:

  • Vice-president of the Israeli society of sexual medicine
  • Israel Urological Association
  • Israel Surgical Association
  • European Association of Urology
  • European Society for Vascular Surgery
  • American Urological Association
  • International Society for Sexual Medicine

In ten years in neurosurgery Dr Rachel Grossman has achieved results that take many a whole career. Thousands of grateful patients, the respect of colleagues, and many awards and research publications make her one of the best in the diagnosis and treatment of brain tumours, not only in Israel but worldwide.

Her education began at Tel Aviv University in 1999. She then took part in research at the University of California, Berkeley, USA, and afterwards completed a fellowship at one of Israel's best-known hospitals. She was trained by leading specialists from London and from the Johns Hopkins hospital in Baltimore.

Dr Grossman researches the treatment of glioma of the brain using pioneering methods and makes active use of nanotechnology in diagnosis. Her research and development work has received support internationally. She is the author of more than 60 research papers and of several chapters in neurosurgical textbooks.

Her contribution to science has been recognised with prestigious prizes, including awards from Johnson & Johnson and from various international associations of neurosurgeons. Her knowledge and experience make her one of the leading specialists in brain diagnosis.

Besides her research, Dr Grossman takes an active part in editing many medical journals and teaches at Tel Aviv University.

EDUCATION

  • Faculty of Medicine, Tel Aviv University, Israel
  • Residency in neurosurgery at the Sheba medical centre (Tel HaShomer), Israel
  • Fellowship in brain tumours at the Johns Hopkins hospital, Baltimore, USA
  • Research work at the University of California, Berkeley, USA
  • International advanced courses in leading technologies for brain surgery, London, England

LANGUAGES

  • Hebrew
  • English

MEMBERSHIP OF INTERNATIONAL ASSOCIATIONS

  • Israel Neurosurgical Society
  • Congress of Neurological Surgeons, USA
  • Society for Neuro-Oncology, USA
